move.why: Softmax runs on the host in every layer and adds host load without placing any KV in memory, so moving it to the fixed-function star unit should cut host time with no capacity risk.

The host is the binding term at 98% of LLM time, and the vocabulary projection is the largest host-resident matrix op; moving lm_head to the crossbar removes it from the host path and fits within the 0.91 GB xbar headroom, though the verifier must confirm capacity.

Attention is the host-bound op and vfu placement was already measured as much slower (131656.9 s), so the untested xbar placement is the next informative way to take q.K^T and p.V off the host; the verifier will show whether xbar_isaac's 1.01 GB headroom holds for the KV appends.

The host is the binding term at 48% of LLM time, and rope is one of the host-side elementwise ops. Moving rope for all 36 layers to vfu removes that host work in one step, which is more informative than the single-layer rule-table candidates.

softmax_star is the binding term at 42% of LLM time, so adding nonlinear unit instances attacks it directly; 16 instances should cut that term by up to 16x, well past the 4 the rule table suggests, and the remaining bottleneck (host, then vfu_puma) becomes visible for the next evaluation.

Host is the binding term and act (SiLU*up) is a nonlinear elementwise op; star is not among the stressed LLM-side terms (vfu_puma is already 1.64x over the next term), so moving act for all layers to star should cut host load without adding pressure to vfu.

vfu_puma is the binding LLM term at 30% of LLM time and is 1.95x above the next term, so a larger vector unit (16 lanes instead of 4) gives the most headroom to move the bottleneck off the vector unit.

Host binds at 21% of LLM time, and the cpu-mapped norm ops are the main host load. qk_norm feeds rope, which already runs on vfu, so moving qk_norm to vfu also removes a cpu-to-vfu transfer (transfer is 19%, 1.37x the next term). Moving attn_norm and mlp_norm too cuts host work across all 36 layers

log.why: Host is the binding term at 100% of LLM time, and attention (q.K^T, p.V, KV appends) is the largest host-side work; moving it to the vfu for all layers removes that load in one evaluation and avoids adding KV pressure to xbar_isaac, which already has the least headroom (0.91 GB).
violations: over capacity from ctx 27129 (pydata__xarray-4094 turn 90); at ctx 65536 needs 9.664e+09 bytes, has 4e+09 (holds kv.K 4.83 GB, kv.V 4.83 GB)

log.why: The illegal proposal put all 36 layers' attention KV on vfu_puma, which overflowed its 4 GB capacity. Moving only layer 0 to vfu keeps KV within capacity while still taking attn_score work off the host, which is the binding term.
